title: AVD Anywhere
subtitle: Azure Virtual Desktop on Azure, Azure Local, and AVD Hybrid Platforms
followAlongPolicy: Full follow-along: every demo has an attendee version. Azure and the portability pattern need no special hardware; Azure Local and Hybrid steps are hypervisor-agnostic with your values as variables.

variables.name: <rg>
variables.meaning: your resource group for the AVD control plane

variables.name: <location>
variables.meaning: an Azure region, for example eastus

variables.name: <user>
variables.meaning: a test user, for example user1@yourtenant.onmicrosoft.com (cloud-only works for Azure Files with Entra Kerberos; an on-site AD share such as a SOFS needs a hybrid user synchronized from AD)

variables.name: <storageaccount>
variables.meaning: a globally unique storage account name for the profile share

variables.name: <profile-share>
variables.meaning: the Azure Files share that holds the profile containers

variables.name: <odfc-share>
variables.meaning: the Azure Files share that holds the Office containers

steps.instructions: List the host pools and the status of their session hosts.
steps.command:
Get-AzWvdHostPool -ResourceGroupName <rg> | Select-Object Name, HostPoolType, LoadBalancerType

demos.title: Sizing AVD on Azure Local: the two public guides and the demo's numbers

followAlong.goal: Size an AVD solution on Azure Local bottom-up for your own users: session hosts and the SOFS that serves the FSLogix profiles.
needs: A browser: https://azurelocal.cloud/azurelocal-avd/ and https://azurelocal.cloud/azurelocal-sofs-fslogix/architecture/capacity-planning/
Your user count, profile size per user type and growth estimate
Your cluster's node count, capacity drives per node and memory per node

steps.title: Read the AVD on Azure Local architecture
steps.instructions: Open https://azurelocal.cloud/azurelocal-avd/ and read the Architecture and Deployment Scenarios pages: session hosts are Azure Local VMs on a logical network, managed from Azure. Pick the scenario closest to yours and size the session hosts from user density (vCPU and memory per user).
steps.check: You have a session-host count and size (vCPU, memory, OS disk) for your users.

steps.title: Size the profile storage
steps.instructions: Open https://azurelocal.cloud/azurelocal-sofs-fslogix/architecture/capacity-planning/ and compare https://azurelocal.cloud/azurelocal-sofs-fslogix/architecture/scenarios/. Compute usable = users × profile size × (1 + growth); guest pool = usable × guest mirror copies; data disks per VM = pool ÷ SOFS VMs; host volume per VM = OS disk + data disks + overhead; raw = host volumes × host mirror copies. Worked example from the session (two hosts): 20 users × 30 GB + 20 % = 720 GB usable → 1.44 TB guest two-way pool → 2 VMs × 4 × 256 GB (one disk per VM kept as repair reserve) → two 1.5 TiB host volumes → 6 TiB raw. On two hosts use two SOFS VMs, one per host, with a cloud witness: a third VM would share a host and losing that host would take the guest quorum.
steps.check: You have usable, guest pool, data-disk, host-volume and raw figures for the profiles.

steps.title: Check the fit on the cluster
steps.instructions: Add the session-host and other VM volumes to the profile volumes, keep one capacity drive per node unallocated as the repair reserve, and check that every VM can restart on the remaining nodes when one node is down (vCPU and memory).
steps.check: Allocated volumes fit inside usable capacity minus the reserve, and the VMs fit on N-1 nodes.

troubleshooting: Raw-to-usable looks far worse than 4:1 at small scale: the fixed OS disks and the second mirror dominate small designs; compare the guide's small-shop scenario.
Does not fit on N-1 nodes: reduce density per host, add a node, or accept that some VMs stay down during a node outage, and write that down.
cleanup: None: nothing is deployed.

demos.title: Plain Hyper-V VMs seen in Azure only as Arc machines

followAlong.goal: Make an ordinary Windows VM on any hypervisor an Arc-enabled server.
needs: A Windows 11 Enterprise VM (any hypervisor)
Rights to onboard Arc machines (Azure Connected Machine Onboarding on the resource group)
Outbound access to the Arc endpoints

steps.title: Create the onboarding principal
steps.instructions: Create a service principal scoped only to the Arc resource group.
steps.command:
$sp = New-AzADServicePrincipal -DisplayName spn-arc-onboard
New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId $sp.Id -RoleDefinitionName 'Azure Connected Machine Onboarding' -Scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<arc rg>
steps.check: The role assignment exists on the Arc resource group.

steps.title: Install and connect the Connected Machine agent in the guest
steps.instructions: In the guest, in an elevated session, download and run AzureConnectedMachineAgent.msi from the Microsoft download link in the Azure Arc documentation, then run the onboarding. Pass the secret in memory and never store it.
steps.check: azcmagent show reports Connected.

troubleshooting: Agent cannot connect: check outbound access to the Arc endpoints and the system clock.
cleanup: azcmagent disconnect, then delete the Arc machine resource.

demos.title: The AVD Hybrid extension on an Arc machine

followAlong.goal: Register an Arc-enabled Windows 11 machine as an AVD Hybrid session host.
needs: A standard host pool created without VMs and with a managed identity
Reader for that identity on the Arc resource group
An Arc-enabled Windows 11 Enterprise VM joined to AD DS, Entra ID or both (hybrid); this demo joins AD DS
Az.DesktopVirtualization and Az.ConnectedMachine

steps.title: Generate a registration token
steps.instructions: Create a short-lived token; keep it in memory only.
steps.check: $token is populated.

steps.title: Install the extension
steps.instructions: Install the AVD Hybrid extension on the Arc machine with the token as a protected setting.
steps.check: The extension shows Succeeded.

steps.title: Wait for the host
steps.instructions: The host can take up to 15 minutes to become Available after the extension succeeds.
steps.check: The host shows Available.

troubleshooting: Host stays Unavailable: confirm Reader for the pool's managed identity on the Arc resource group and outbound access to the AVD service URLs.

demos.title: Identity: three paths, one proof

followAlong.goal: Enable Entra Kerberos on an Azure Files share and confirm a Windows 11 Entra-joined VM obtains a ticket.
needs: An Entra-joined Windows 11 VM
A storage account (FileStorage or StorageV2) with a file share
Rights to grant admin consent
Note: cloud-only identities are supported (GA) for Azure Files with Entra Kerberos; check the current Windows 11 build requirement on Microsoft Learn

steps.title: Enable Entra Kerberos on the storage account
steps.instructions: In the portal: Storage account > File shares > Identity-based access > Microsoft Entra Kerberos > Set up. Enable it, then grant admin consent to the generated app registration.
steps.check: An app named [Storage Account] <storageaccount>.file.core.windows.net exists with consent granted.

steps.title: Allow the ticket to be issued without MFA
steps.instructions: Exclude the storage account's app from Conditional Access policies that require MFA; the ticket request is silent and cannot prompt.
steps.check: The app appears under Exclude in the policy.

steps.title: Enable cloud-only group support
steps.instructions: In the app registration manifest add the tag kdc_enable_cloud_group_sids. Use security groups that are not nested.
steps.check: The tag appears in the manifest tags array.

steps.title: Enable ticket retrieval on the client
steps.instructions: Set the registry value that lets the client request the Entra Kerberos ticket and restart the client.
steps.check: Value is 1.

steps.title: Assign share-level permission
steps.instructions: Assign Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor to your users group on the share.
steps.command: New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId <group object id> -RoleDefinitionName 'Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor' -Scope <share resource id>
steps.check: The role assignment lists on the share.

steps.title: Request the ticket
steps.instructions: Restart the client, then sign in again to the VM as an Entra user (the registry value takes effect at sign-in) and request a ticket for the storage account.
steps.check: klist shows a ticket for the cifs service of the storage account.

troubleshooting: No ticket: check the client is Entra-joined or hybrid-joined, the registry value, and the MFA exclusion.
Access denied after the ticket: check the share-level role and the NTFS ACL.
cleanup: Remove the role assignment and disable Entra Kerberos on the storage account if it was a test.

demos.title: Security across the three terminals: one portal walk

followAlong.goal: Check the same security controls on your own AVD environment.
needs: An AVD host pool with session hosts (Azure VMs and/or Arc-enabled machines)
Microsoft Defender for Cloud with Defender for Servers and Defender for Storage on the subscriptions
A Log Analytics workspace with Microsoft Sentinel and Windows security events collected by the Azure Monitor Agent

steps.title: Host pool: device redirection
steps.instructions: Azure Virtual Desktop > Host pools > your pool > RDP Properties > Device redirection: turn off what you do not need (drives, printers, cameras, smart cards).
steps.check: CustomRdpProperty contains drivestoredirect:s:; redirectprinters:i:0; camerastoredirect:s:

steps.title: Defender for Cloud: plans and inventory
steps.instructions: Defender for Cloud > Environment settings > your subscription: Servers Plan 2 and Storage On. Then Inventory, search for your hosts.
steps.command: Get-AzSecurityPricing | Where-Object PricingTier -eq Standard | Select-Object Name, SubPlan
steps.check: VirtualMachines Standard P2 and StorageAccounts Standard DefenderForStorageV2; every session host is listed in Inventory.

steps.title: Sentinel: security events per host
steps.instructions: Log Analytics workspace > Logs: run the step 4 query with your host name prefix.
steps.command: SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h) | where Computer has "<host prefix>" | summarize count() by Computer
steps.check: One row per session host.

troubleshooting: A host missing from SecurityEvent: check that it is associated with the Windows security events data collection rule and that the Azure Monitor Agent extension succeeded.

An Arc machine without MDE.Windows: Defender for Servers onboards Defender for Endpoint on supported server and multi-session operating systems; onboard single-session Windows client machines with Intune or the Defender for Endpoint onboarding package.
cleanup: Nothing to clean up (read-only).

demos.title: Connecting flight 2: the user is entitled to the right terminal

followAlong.goal: Control which desktop a user sees with group membership.

A test user

steps.title: Add the user to the first group

demos.title: Connecting flight 4: forced host failure on Hybrid

followAlong.goal: See what a host failure does to a session and what survives.
needs: A host pool with two Available hosts (VMs you can stop)
FSLogix profile on shared storage
A test user with a session

steps.title: Start a session and leave an unsaved document open
steps.instructions: Sign in and open a document without saving it.
steps.check: The session is on host 1.

steps.title: Stop host 1 hard
steps.instructions: Stop the VM without a graceful shutdown (for a Hyper-V VM: Stop-VM -TurnOff).
steps.check: The host shows Unavailable in the pool after a minute or two.

steps.title: Open a new session
steps.instructions: Reconnect from Windows App; the broker sends you to host 2.
steps.check: You are on host 2; your saved files and settings are present; the unsaved document is not.

steps.title: Restart host 1
steps.instructions: Start the VM; AVD does not do this for you in a Hybrid host pool.
steps.check: The host returns to Available.

troubleshooting: Profile will not attach: a stale handle on the container; wait for the SMB session to expire or close the handle on the share.
cleanup: Ensure both hosts are Available.

demos.title: Connecting flight 6: the Observability Agent explains the failure (preview)

followAlong.goal: Investigate an Azure Monitor alert with the Azure Copilot Observability Agent (preview) and keep the result as an issue.
needs: Access to Azure Copilot in your tenant
An Azure Monitor workspace associated with the subscription (it holds the issues)
Issue Contributor, Monitoring Contributor or Contributor on that workspace
A fired Azure Monitor alert, for example a session-host alert, in a region where the agent is available

steps.title: Start an investigation from an alert
steps.instructions: Open a fired alert in Azure Monitor > Alerts and select Investigate. Confirm the scope the agent proposes.
steps.check: The agent reports its plan, then findings, hypotheses ruled out and next steps.

steps.title: Keep the result
steps.instructions: Select Create issue to save the investigation as an Azure Monitor issue in your Azure Monitor workspace.
steps.check: The issue is listed under Monitor > Issues with the investigation attached.

troubleshooting: Asked for an Azure Monitor workspace: associate the subscription with one (once per subscription).
No Investigate action: check that your account has Azure Copilot access.
cleanup: Close or delete test issues; chat and investigations are billed per use.
